title: Commutator Geometry and Information Preservation in the Quantum Switch
abstract: Two commuting channels yield the same composite channel in either fixed order, yet their quantum switch can alter information preservation. We study how this effect depends on the input state, retaining the joint output of the control and target. Exact Kraus commutator identities determine overlap and squared fidelity gaps. Fixed order preserves product inputs at least as well as the switch in fidelity. The reverse inequality holds for pure states of two qubits whose control Schmidt basis can be chosen to coincide with the order basis. A commutator matrix determines the target basis that maximizes the squared fidelity gap at fixed entanglement within this aligned family. For Pauli $X$ and $Y$ channels with equal error probabilities, the switch replaces a logical phase flip with an operator that stabilizes a joint code. At fixed noise, the switch preserves at least as much distinguishability and quantum Fisher information as fixed order for every state family in this code. For the pure encoded family studied here, exact formulas connect the phase information gain to the squared fidelity gap and quantify the reduction in information about the noise probability. Optimizing the probes yields equal maximal quantum Fisher information for noise estimation under both joint channels. These results connect commutator geometry and logical error structure to state preservation and the retention of encoded information.
summary: This theoretical work investigates the difference in information preservation when quantum channels are applied via a 'quantum switch' versus a fixed sequence. By using commutator geometry, the authors derive quantitative bounds showing how the switch affects fidelity and Quantum Fisher Information. The findings connect fundamental algebraic structures to the robustness of quantum information encoding against noise.
main_problem: The paper compares how information preservation (fidelity, QFI) differs when two commuting quantum channels are applied in a quantum switch versus a fixed sequential order.
main_result: For product inputs, the switch preserves fidelity at least as well as the fixed order; however, the gap is quantified by commutator identities, showing complex dependencies on the input state and channel structure.
method: The analysis uses operator sum descriptions, commutator identities, and root fidelity to derive exact mathematical relationships between the output states of the two operational orders.
model_or_system: The model involves two commuting quantum channels acting on a joint system, analyzed using concepts from quantum error correction (e.g., Pauli codes) and quantum metrology.
key_observables: Fidelity gap ($F_{FO} - F_{SW}$), Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), distinguishability, and commutator components ($Q_{ij}$).
important_parameters: Input state ($ho$), channel parameters (e.g., error probabilities for Pauli X/Y channels), and the structure of the joint code.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to two commuting channels and often assumes specific product or pure encoded state families for deriving exact formulas.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the fidelity gap ($\Delta P$) for Pauli X and Y channels as a function of input orientation and control angle, showing distinct gain/loss regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the comparison between switch and fixed order, deriving commutator identities, establishing monotonicity for product states, and finally connecting the fidelity gap to QFI gain for pure encoded families.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical tools (commutator geometry) to quantify the advantage or disadvantage of indefinite causal order in noisy quantum processes, which is highly relevant for quantum communication protocols.
